sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204 to 1760
sources.note: Full University of California Press scholarly edition read; chapters on riverine geography, agrarian expansion and women's work. Used sparingly across public text.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Bengal i: Persian Muslim elements in the history of Bengal
sources.note: Original scholarly article read: Husayn Shahi dynasty c.1493, Mughal conquest 1576, resistance of local chiefs through 1613, Indo-Persian cultural evidence.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Mughal Mosques in Bangladesh
sources.note: Government nomination read directly. Historical narrative paragraph: 1576 nominal incorporation, 1609 eastern consolidation and Dhaka capital, 1666 Chattagram; nomination is a proposal, not an inscribed property.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Historic Mosque City of Bagerhat
sources.note: Inscribed site account read directly: fifteenth-century Khalifatabad, brick roads, bridges, water tanks, reservoirs and mosque groups. Page typo '15th century BC' ignored; historical dating follows AD elsewhere on page.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Dedicatory Inscription from a Mosque, 1500
sources.note: Direct museum object record 1981.320: western Bengal, Prince Daniyal, 905 AH/1500 CE, local tughra-style carving. Museum page identifies object but does not publish full original-script transcription.

sources.title: Maryam D. Ekhtiar, How to Read Islamic Calligraphy, Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.note: Met original publication; printed discussion of Prince Daniyal inscription confirmed from indexed book excerpt; translated building clause and tughra design. Exact Arabic transcription independently checked against Commons image description, separately credited.

sources.title: Wikimedia Commons, transcription and photograph of Prince Daniyal inscription
sources.note: Public-domain museum object photograph and a community-supplied full Arabic transcription; cite alongside Met object and publication. Text has not been independently deciphered from stone, so public passage calls this a published transcription rather than autographic reading.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Panel from a Mantle or Apron
sources.note: Direct original object record: Bengal Satgaon-Hugli, early seventeenth century; cotton and tasar silk; mermaids, hunters, European figures and mixed models.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Coverlet (Colcha), Bengal
sources.note: Direct object essay: Satgaon seventeenth-century export cotton/tasar coverlets for Portuguese market, scenes from biblical, classical and Hindu narratives, high prices in England. Caveat against treating export piece as ordinary bedding.

sources.title: Durham University, Varendra Research Museum Arabic inscription of Husayn Shah
sources.note: University museum object VRM2913, Ulipur, Kurigram, Alauddin Husayn Shah; direct open unavailable, indexed original description checked. Supports courtly writing presence, not exact transcription.

sources.title: Thowhidul Islam, Educational System in Muslim Bengal under the Sultanate
sources.note: Original peer-reviewed article abstract read: scholar-led majlis teaching religious law, logic, mathematics and medicine in selected institutions. Does not quantify broad literacy or school attendance.

sources.title: Shireen Moosvi, The World of Labour in Mughal India
sources.note: Original scholarly article indexed full text; women's agricultural and textile work in wider Mughal India, contextual rather than direct Bengal census evidence.

sources.title: Cambridge University Press, Bengal rice export chronology
sources.note: Scholarly book front matter chronology directly indexed; sixteenth-century Bengal rice shipped to the Moluccas, Maldives and Goa.

proposedOverrides.summary: A Bengal map label spanning the late independent sultanate, Afghan and local resistance, and Mughal provincial rule; eastern borders in the imported snapshots are unreliable.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact imported bengal record covers 1492 to 1650. Decoded 1492/1500 polygons span 82.55 to 92.03 E and 19.61 to 27.00 N, while 1530/1600 polygons shrink to 84.69 to 90.00 E and 19.61 to 24.87 N, excluding Dhaka. Neither is a researched border. Historical political phases cross independent sultanate, Afghan contest and Mughal province; no geometry was altered.
